subject: Orbit Health — interoperability & SLO comparison follow-up and next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <aporter@orbithealth.com>, Dr. Nina Rao <nina.rao@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Orbit Health — interoperability & SLO comparison follow-up and next tests

Alex / Nina — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the evaluation scope: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: embed summarization + reranking into clinical docs workflow with predictable 99th percentile latency under 300ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens) and throughput >= 60 qps for batch inference.
- Primary concerns: tail latency, rate limits under burst loads, and deterministic failover across regions (US-east fallback).
- Procurement/terms will want SOC 2 evidence and a clear SLA for uptime / error budget handling.

Competitive context we discussed
- You mentioned tests vs MajorCloud endpoints and a self-hosted baseline. On the call we flagged: MajorCloud shows variable tail latency at production scale and opaque rate-limit windows; self-hosted has lower per-token cost but higher ops overhead.
- Redwood differentiators: predictable latency at the tail through continuous batching + dynamic kernel selection, prefix KV caching for repeated clinical templates, and explicit multi-variant failover policies (region + quantized fallback).

Proposed technical tests (owner / timeline)
1) Tail latency probe: synthetic 60 qps steady-state + 300 qps 30s burst, capture p50/p95/p99 latency and error rates (Owner: Ben; target: 2026-12-07)
2) Rate-limit stress: push sustained QPS above configured request rate windows to validate backpressure vs 429 behavior and retry windows (Owner: Ben; target: 2026-12-09)
3) Failover rehearsal: simulate single-region outage and validate cross-region splicing and model-variant fallback (Owner: Marissa; target: 2026-12-10)
4) SOC2 & evidence handoff: provide SOC2 summary and audit artifacts; procurement to list required artifacts (Owner: Marissa/Procurement; target: 2026-12-03)

Attachments included: the SLO comparison workbook and the proposed failover probe plan.

Next immediate ask from Orbit: please confirm the telemetry fields you need in the probe logs (latency buckets, request id, tenant id, model variant) and confirm procurement contact for SOC2 delivery.

Best,
Marissa

Date: 2026-11-30T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orbit Health — interoperability & SLO comparison follow-up and next tests

Marissa — solid recap, thank you. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Telemetry fields: we need request_id, tenant_id, model_variant, latency_ms (raw and bucketed at 10/50/100/300/500/1000 bins), http_status, and the server-region tag. Can you confirm Redwood can emit those fields in the probe payload?

2) For the tail-latency probe: will Redwood run the probe tooling or do you want Orbit to run it from our CI agents? We can run from three egress points in NY, CA, and EU to validate client-side latency too.

3) Procurement contact: procurement@orbithealth.com (cc'd) — they will send a list of SOC2 artifacts. Can you send the SOC2 summary PDF today so we can start legal?

Also, for the MajorCloud comparison, could you provide any anonymized p99 numbers you have from similar healthcare workloads to orient expectations? MajorCloud is quoting 450-600ms p99 under load, which would be too high for our use case.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Porter
Product Manager, Integrations | Orbit Health
aporter@orbithealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <aporter@orbithealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dr. Nina Rao <nina.rao@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orbit Health — interoperability & SLO comparison follow-up and next tests

Alex — we can emit all of those fields. Quick technical notes on the probes: 

- Telemetry: request_id, tenant_id, model_variant, latency_ms (raw), http_status, server_region, and queue_time_ms are standard for our probe mode. We can also include a boolean for cache_hit when prefix KV caching triggers.
- Tail-latency probe ownership: Redwood can run a coordinated probe from our test harness (Ben's team) and we'll accept client-originated probes as well. I recommend we both run the test in parallel for one run to compare client-side network variance vs server-side.
- p99 numbers: attached sheet includes anonymized p99s for a healthcare-like workload (short clinical prompts) across MajorCloud and self-hosted baselines. TL;DR: MajorCloud p99s in our dataset were 360-520ms depending on region; our quantized low-latency variant sits at 220-280ms p99 under 60 qps with optimized kernel selection.

Planned run details (we'll post results to the Drive link by 2026-12-08):
- Run A: steady 60 qps for 30m, measure p50/p95/p99, error-rate, retry count.
- Run B: 30s 300 qps burst on top of Run A baseline.
- Run C: controlled 429 gating test to validate backpressure behavior and consistent retry-after headers.

I'll attach the anonymized p99 chart and the probe config.

Ben
